source: Members from rba.gov.au (2 Oct 2026). Scores: the desk's read as at the 29 Sep 2026 decision, sourced in each note; members with no on-record view are placed at the Board's revealed (unanimous) position.
note: The RBA publishes only an UNATTRIBUTED vote count, so no score here can be checked against a named vote: each is the desk's read from the member's own on-record remarks (cited in the note), and members who have said nothing on rates sit at the Board's revealed position. Re-mark them from speeches as they come (the Vote count tab's speech roundup writes back). 5 = most hawkish.

voters.name: Michele Bullock
voters.note: Hawkish, data-led. 29 Sep media conference: 'The Board will increase interest rates again if that's what's needed'; unemployment 'a bit tight'; hopes 4.60% is 'restrictive enough'. rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/mc-gov-2026-09-29.html

voters.name: Andrew Hauser
voters.note: Most hawkish on the record: inflation the economy's 'one big problem'; rates would rise 'further than otherwise' if expectations slip, 'not at that point yet' (ABC 7.30, 8 Sep 2026). rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/sp-dg-2026-09-08.html

voters.name: Jenny Wilkinson
voters.note: No on-record view on rates in 2026. Placed at the Board's revealed position: the 29 Sep hike was unanimous (9-0). Imputed from the published vote, not the member.

voters.name: Melinda Cilento
voters.note: Joined 1 Sep 2026 (ex-CEDA CEO). Public comment on productivity and AI, none on rates; voted in the unanimous 29 Sep hike. Placed at the Board's revealed position.

voters.name: Carolyn Hewson
voters.note: Credibility-first: 'inflation expectations are better when anchored. Policy credibility is stronger' (speech, 27 May 2026); no rate call. rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/sp-mpb-2026-05-27.html

voters.name: Iain Ross
voters.note: Least hawkish on the record: 'little evidence that a self-sustaining wage-price spiral has emerged'; labour market easing towards balance (speech, 22 Sep 2026). Still voted for the 29 Sep hike. rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/sp-mpb-2026-09-22.html
